In response to [this](https://github.com/openshift/oauth-server/pull/244):

>When `PROXY_TRUSTED_CA_FILE` is set, the OAuth Server watches the proxy CA file on disk and rebuilds outbound HTTP transports when it changes. The proxy CA is combined with any static IdP CA in the transport's RootCAs, so TLS-intercepting or HTTPS proxies are trusted alongside IdP endpoints.
>
>The `dynamicCARoundTripper` uses `DynamicFileCAContent` (fsnotify + periodic poll) and swaps the underlying transport atomically. On reload failure the old transport is preserved.

```
In `@pkg/oauthserver/dynamic_transport_test.go`:
- Around line 126-127: The test in dynamic_transport_test is ignoring errors
from http.NewRequest, which violates the never-ignore-errors rule. Update each
request construction site in this test file to use http.NewRequestWithContext
with t.Context(), check the returned error, and fail the test immediately if
request creation fails before calling rt.RoundTrip or any similar helper.

In `@pkg/oauthserver/dynamic_transport.go`:
- Around line 69-82: The buildTransport method in dynamicCARoundTripper
currently creates a fresh cert pool and assigns it to tls.Config.RootCAs, which
replaces the system trust store when only PROXY_TRUSTED_CA_FILE is set. Update
buildTransport to start from the host/system roots and then append
rt.proxyCAContent.CurrentCABundleContent() (and any IdP certs) so public-CA IdPs
remain trusted; keep the existing error handling around parsing the proxy
bundle.
```
